notes_8ymewr: batch: await-family unlock (all edits in src/selfhost/ngen_async.zan). (1) await of a delegate VALUE (local/field/parameter -- the Worker.onDown family): IsDelegateCalleeNg promotes the AsyncResolveCallNg -1 fallback to -2 ONLY on the await paths (EmitAwaitNg head + TryGenAwaitExprNg sync path); the thunk dispatches to the method-group ramp yielding the frame handle and the general await reads SELF resume from the frame. Placing the check INSIDE AsyncResolveCallNg was a real bug caught by the sweep: PrepareAsyncStmtNg (Hook B, detach recognition) runs AsyncResolveCallNg on EVERY call statement, so delegate-valued statements like `sink(3);` were emitted as detached async calls and the void thunk return was later dereferenced as a frame handle (delegate_field_call SIGSEGV, 8 em + 2 om regressions + spurious co-runtime emission in non-async modules). Restored: pass 286 (+2), em/om/mne case lists identical to the run.OniEz2 baseline. (2) self-lowered suspension intrinsics (CoIntrinsicKindNg/EmitCoIntrinsicNg, IR-lane EmitSocketIntrinsic as spec): Gate.Park, Socket.ReadReady/WriteReady (immediate-ready on the native lane; interest 1/2 constant), RecvOv/RecvToOv (one libc recv, negative errno-style return propagates, timeout not enforced - documented), AcceptOv (libc accept, fails closed), ResolveSockAddr (IPv4 literal -> 16-byte darwin sockaddr_in via inet_pton, DNS names -> *outn=0 documented gap). resUsed=true is an error for the valueless kinds; value kinds deliver the frame+32 result slot. (3) the gate/io runtime is self-emitted inside EnsureAsyncRuntimeNg (guarded by asyncRtDone) so the DllImport EntryPoints (zan_gate_new/signal/free) bind locally: BLExtern scans local syms first. Gate = {head,tail,surplus} 24B, waiter {next,frame,step} 24B, surplus banking semantics per rt_io.c 5060-5160; gate_free drains waiters (no free on the native lane). Bugs found by probes: park enqueue kept the gate in x0 across the _zan_rt_alloc call (return value clobbered it - waiter self-looped, Signal never woke it; fixed by spilling the gate), and rev16 was encoded as REV (0x5AC00C21 vs 0x5AC00421) - SIGILL inside _zan_resolve_sa_co. Probes: delegate await local+field (qa1), Gate park/signal/surplus/closed round trip (qa2), recv/accept -1 propagation + sockaddr bytes 16,2,31,144,127 for 127.0.0.1:8080 + DNS -> 0 (qa3) all correct. chart_kinds_complete honest profile (run from zan-selfhost so the stdlib resolves; the earlier 34-error reading was an artifact of running from tests/conformance where the relative-stdlib fallback finds nothing): 81 -> 44. Remaining chart families: Get$T explicit generic specs (8), delegate capture/7-param shapes (6), Html Dictionary<Action> (3), awaited DllImports NativeResolveAllAsync/NativeConnectSockAddr (2, blocking-extern lowering per irgen_expr.c:7969), FindNotAnyOf (2), Task.Delay-arg + ToStr-arity cascades, Interop Com. notes_dfN3PV: batch: thread-runtime unlock, three parts. (1) crt-transition/zanstubs.c grew the 45 Threading DllImport symbols, semantics ported from oracle src/runtime/rt_sync.c: zan_thread_start (pthread_create detached; our lane's ThreadStart delegate object is {fn@0, env@8}, invoked fn(env), no refcounting - nm confirms the lane has no _zan_delegate_* refs) + zan_thread_current_id (pthread_threadid_np, same as the oracle's macOS branch); 7 zan_atomic_int_* (C11 __atomic SEQ_CST on a malloc'd int64; add returns the new value, compare_exchange returns the old); 36 zan_shared_table_* as a single-process honest port (in-memory named registry + heap columnar rows; schema 'i:n;/'f:n;'/'s:size:n;' with string size+1 for the NUL exactly like zan_parse_schema, duplicate columns rejected, int/float align8; FNV-1a 64 forced-nonzero hashing shared by hash() and the _at family; wall-clock expiry with oracle purge semantics; rate_allow/lock_acquire/lock_release/extreme_at/match_at algorithms ported line-by-line incl. the INT 'count'/'window_start'/'owner' columns and create-only-if-absent locking; 7/8 load-factor insert refusal; stat maps RESERVED/RESIDENT to stride*cap, honest -1/0/empty-string on misses; OsHandle/Attach fail cleanly = 0 since the transition runtime has no cross-process carrier; tables deliberately never freed so handles can't dangle). (2) PER-THREAD EH: exception_threads caught _zan_rt_eh_state caching its state block behind one process-global - with real threads a thread could longjmp into a slot armed by another thread. RtEmitEhState (ngen_obj.zan) now just tail-calls the new zan_eh_tls_state in zanstubs.c (static __thread storage, same compiler-owned {i32 top, ptr exc, 256x1024} layout; scripts/crossboot/stub.c serves a static block for the single-threaded qemu guest). Mach-O extern names need the leading underscore in BLExtern - the no-underscore spelling broke every link until fixed (ELF strips exactly one underscore, so one spelling serves both). (3) REAL lock MONITORING: monitor_striped exposed the parser lowering `lock (e) body` to a plain block (written pre-threads). Parser now emits AK.LockStmt; ngen GenLockStmt desugars after checking to { var $lockN = obj; monitor_enter($lockN); try body finally monitor_exit($lockN) } over the striped recursive zan_monitor_enter/exit ported from rt_sync.c (64 stripes, pointer-fold hash, re-entrancy legal). Riding the real try machinery gives the oracle's exact release discipline (irgen_stmt.c AST_LOCK_STMT): throw releases at the throw site, return/break/continue via the pending-fin walk, nested unwind lands in the lock's own armed buf. Two ngen bugs found by probes and fixed: (a) the lock temp slot was added during emission, after frame = 16*nloc froze - it wrote outside the frame (qa4/qa11/qa13 SEGV, probe bisection: inline loop fine, loop-in-method + later try crashed); fixed by allocating the slot in ReserveLocals' LockStmt arm and stashing the decl node in s.c; (b) HasTry didn't see LockStmt, so curHasTry stayed false and the #ehtop/#ehbase/#ehbrk slots + state-top mirror init were skipped entirely; HasTry now counts LockStmt. Probes: qa4 (single-thread lock/reentrancy/throw-release), qa5 (plain nested try/finally baseline), qa6 (real try/finally inside lock), qa8 (lock no-throw + throw shapes), qa10/qa11/qa12/qa13 (loop x300/x1000 inline vs cross-method) all byte-exact; monitor_striped 40000/40000/reentrant x3 stable. notes_00JWPU: batch: Get$T explicit-generic spec calls. CollectSpecsInEnvNg's two SpecRegister paths looked generics up by GLOBAL bare name (FindGenericDecl, first match wins): explicit type args and first-argument inference hijacked same-named members of unrelated classes - Control.Get<T>(name) hijacked Com.Get(iface,index) (371 chart 'too many arguments calling Get$nint') and JsonValue.Get(key) ('unknown static method Get$string'). notes_gHqSU9: batch: per-instantiation generic-class ctor specialization. Generic-class ctors were compiled once, open, with erasure: any type-sensitive lowering inside them degraded to the reference shape - new Dict<T,int>() inside HashSet<T>'s ctor kept the dict key-kind bits clear (string mode), so int-key instantiations strcmp'd their keys (hashset_basic segfault, qa22 Bag<int> repro). GenNew now routes generic-class news through InstCtorSpecNg: clone the open ctor, drop TypeParam kids, SubstTypeNode with the instantiation args, AddMethNg under the OPEN class (stat 2, sval2=instName types `this` so field accesses substitute), emit BLInternal under a per-instantiation symbol. EmitMethod mirrors the symbol via CtorSpecSymOf (multi-ctor classes append substituted param tags exactly like CtorSymNg - first draft omitted the tags and Transfer<string> failed to link, caught by the chart profile before ship). CtorCountNg and FitCtorIdx ignore sval2 ctors so clone registration can never flip the open class's single-vs-multi mangling or hijack open ctor resolution. Field initializers lower through the same open nodes, so the ctor prologue substitutes a clone for spec'd ctors. LIMITATIONS (documented, none exercised by the suite): `: this(...)` chains inside a spec'd ctor target the open sibling; generic BASE class ctor chains still run the open base ctor. Also noted: Console.WriteLine(<direct spec'd-method call>) types the argument int instead of bool at the overload pick (prints 1/0 for true/false; value correct; pre-dates this batch, unexercised - hashset_basic wraps in Convert.ToString). Sweep 306->307: hashset_basic em->pass, zero regressions; chart profile byte-identical (2138, no delta).
notes_7mjxpH: batch: the 8 om/em timeout socket cases (async_asocket_echo, async_socket_async_echo, ipv6, accept_after_close, async_concurrent_echo, async_dns, async_mt, socket_close_wakes) moved onto the real IO reactor. Four honest-suspension gaps closed: (1) readiness gating - recv_co/recv_to_co/accept_co probe with a zero-timeout pollfd before their syscall (zt_fd_ready) because accepted sockets are often left blocking-mode and one blocking recv froze the single-threaded engine (socket_close_wakes, sample: __recvfrom); (2) dead-fd fast fail mirroring oracle io_reject_dead_fd - wait/recv deliver 0 and accept delivers -1 immediately for a non-alive fd instead of parking it; decisive on macOS where stdlib CreateTcp6/CreateUdp6 use Linux socket(10,..) (Darwin AF_INET6=30) so every v6 fd is -1 and poll() silently ignores negative fds - a parked watch never fires (lldb: fd=-1 kind=W); ipv6 now reproduces the oracle's exact observable behavior line 'FAIL reply= rc=-1 got= peer= salen=16' (stale oracle v6 connect is the spec here); (3) DNS self-pipe read end set O_NONBLOCK - the poll-side drain loop blocked forever on the byte after the last byte of a blocking pipe; (4) Socket.ResolveAsync lowered as compiler intrinsic kind 7 -> _zan_resolve_ipv4_co: the stdlib body awaits ITSELF (self-recursion stub), the oracle lowers it to zan_io_resolve_co (empty name -> immediate *out=0, else worker delivers zan_io_resolve_ipv4's int); without it async_dns/async_mt recursed through the scheduler forever. Emitter side: _zan_io_poll hooked into _zan_co_sched_run_until between timers_due and the timer sleep; _zan_co_ready self-registers via the zan_co_ready_hook function pointer (weak symbols unusable with macOS ld static links); ngen_macho ExternSyms collects undefined non-GOT data strRefs so the hook pointer's adrp+add relocation resolves.
